kyoto_takahitori.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: ponzu, homemade soy-sauce koji, white-miso and dashi dishes (2025 reviews); no allergen information.
kyoto_takahitori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a duck restaurant — duck meat, offal and duck broth (official site; reviews).
kyoto_takahitori.hours_raw: Official site and Tabelog: 17:00–23:00; closed Tuesday and Wednesday. 7 counter seats, run by the owner alone (official site) — phone ahead to check for a seat (official site); fully booked nights (November 2025). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Non-smoking throughout. Basement of the House 24 building, beneath the coffee shop MIWAKU, on the southwest side of Yodobashi Camera (Tabelog). Opening: Tabelog says 16 June 2014; the official site says June of Heisei 27 (2015).
kyoto_takahitori.notes: [Kyoto sake and duck · Kyoto Station, a one-man basement counter] A seven-seat basement counter by Kyoto Station where the owner, alone, pours sake from every one of Kyoto Prefecture's 40 breweries in small measures with the story of each, alongside Kyo-Tamba duck from tongue to tenderloin. Portions are small (August 2026); a little hard to find and to walk into. Call ahead. Cash only. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.

roles: Owner, running the shop alone (official site)
chef_bio.background: Per the official site, owner 川嶋隆徳 runs the seven-seat counter alone, pairing Kyoto sake with Kyo-duck raised in Kyotamba, and stocks sake from all 40 breweries in Kyoto Prefecture, large and small. Diners in 2024–2026 describe a basement counter close to the owner, careful explanations of each brewery, rare duck cuts, and mostly solo guests.
chef_bio.philosophy: From the official site: Kyoto sake for visitors and locals alike — "京都の日本酒にこだわり" (particular about Kyoto sake).

anecdotes.text: November 2025: a sake from the Shotoku brewery in Fushimi "available only at this restaurant, filled with nitrogen" — and when the guest ordered a second glass of the same sake, the owner "kindly changed the sake cup."
May 2025: "Since the owner operates the restaurant solo, I want to be a considerate customer who can read the room… and not linger unnecessarily."
August 2026: "The portions are small, but they are unique delicacies that pair perfectly with drinks."

kyoto_kamehachi_honten.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: miso and soy broths; the finishing noodles are domestic wheat with tapioca; nama-fu, chijimi and karaage on the menu (official site).
kyoto_kamehachi_honten.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef-offal hot pot in dashi; horse sashimi, smoked mackerel (official site).
kyoto_kamehachi_honten.hours_raw: Official site and Tabelog: 17:00–24:00 (last orders food 23:00, drinks 23:30); open all year except irregular days (New Year, staff training). Two-hour limit when busy. Book through the official site (24 hours; the phone is often busy); weekends fill up, and winter is hard to book (official site). Table charge ¥380 incl. tax, an otoshi of smoked mackerel — Tabelog, Japanese original 「チャージ料 税込380円（付出し）」. 30 seats: counters, tables and tatami rooms; upstairs for groups to 20. Non-smoking (and no smoking outside). Children welcome. Cards (Visa, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR. Down the alley east of Kiyamachi Rokkaku, halfway along Pontocho 5th alley. Opened 1 April 2008 (official site; Tabelog).
kyoto_kamehachi_honten.notes: [Motsu-nabe · Pontocho alley, Kyoto white-miso hot pot] The original shop (2008) of a three-shop Kyoto motsu-nabe house, tucked in an alley between Kiyamachi and Pontocho: Omi beef offal in a Kyoto dashi broth — the white-miso version is the one to order — finished with stone-ground noodles or egg zosui, and all-you-can-drink courses from ¥5,000. Book on the website; winter fills. ¥380 table charge.

roles: Second-generation manager known in the shop as "Pe-san" (official site); owner not named
chef_bio.background: Per the official site, 亀八 本店 opened in April 2008 as the first shop; the name pairs 亀 (turtle, for luck) and 八 (eight, for endless happiness). Early on the first manager stood outside every day calling in customers; word of mouth made it so busy that winter tables could not be booked, without spending on advertising. The second-generation manager, a regular of a sister shop since university who joined in 2009 and worked at the annex 亀八別館 first, keeps the founding recipe (official site). Sister shops: 亀八別館 (Pontocho) and 亀八 山科店 (official site).
chef_bio.philosophy: From the site: a hot pot that starts from taking dashi, the heart of Kyoto cooking — "a hot pot made for drinking the soup" (official site, translated).

anecdotes.text: August 2026: at the counter, "the manager and staff shared delicious ways to enjoy the food," and the white broth used a Kyoto ginjo white miso.
July 2026: the "ultimate noodles" "had a slightly junky flavor."

kyoto_bifuu_tainan_tears2.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles, scallion pancakes, dan bing, fried pork chop; soy-braised dishes (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_bifuu_tainan_tears2.vegan_detail: Not vegan: lu rou fan, beef noodle soup, pork rib and chicken bento (2025–2026 reviews).
kyoto_bifuu_tainan_tears2.hours_raw: Tabelog: 12:00–15:00 and 18:00–22:00; closed Monday. Rurubu gives 12:00–14:30 (last order 14:15) and 18:00–21:30 (last order 21:00), closed Monday (Tuesday if Monday is a holiday) and the first Tuesday. No reservations — queues form before opening on Saturdays (April and October 2026); orders are taken from whoever calls first, not in queue order, and food can be slow at peak (2026 reviews). 28 seats: a dirt-floor front room and a tatami room at the back of a townhouse. Non-smoking; children and strollers welcome; take-away. No cards; e-money and PayPay.
kyoto_bifuu_tainan_tears2.notes: [Taiwanese · Kawaramachi-Marutamachi, Tainan diner in a townhouse] A retro Tainan-style diner in an old townhouse just north of Kawaramachi-Marutamachi, run largely by Taiwanese students: lu rou fan, beef noodle soup, pork-chop fried rice, rib bento and douhua at under ¥1,000 a dish. It fills within minutes of opening; orders go to whoever calls first and can be slow (2026); portions are on the small side (April 2026). No bookings, no cards. Closed Monday.

chef_bio.background: A 2017 nippon.com column describes a small, plain sign reading 微風台南 near the Imperial Palace, a blackboard of Taiwanese bento, Taiwanese soft drinks on old wooden tables, a red lantern and a Tainan shop sticker on the door. Rurubu says nearly all the part-time staff are Taiwanese students. Reviewers in 2024–2026 describe a townhouse with an earth-floored front and a tatami room at the back, Taiwanese-accented staff and many Taiwanese customers.
chef_bio.specialty: Lu rou fan; braised beef noodle soup.

anecdotes.text: October 2026: by 11:55 "there were already 6 to 7 groups lined up… be aware that they don't take orders in the order of the line… They take orders based on who calls the staff first."

November 2026: "The seasoning was neither particularly good nor bad… more like the flavor level you'd find in a student area!" — but the bai tang guo tasted "almost exactly like what I had for breakfast near National Taiwan University."
April 2026: "Each dish was a bit on the smaller side."
